source.title: An active inference approach to modeling structure learning: concept learning as an example case

confidence_rationale: Direction convention: 'weakens' = weakens the distinct-novel-object reading. This paper delivers capacity (c) -- latent-node birth/death/merge/split -- INSIDE active inference: state-space expansion adds new hidden causes (birth/split), Bayesian model reduction merges/prunes redundant states (death/merge), and the two combine for online structure learning. It also touches (d): hierarchical concept differentiation (basic -> subordinate categories) is granularity adjustment within the same model. That places (c), and a first cut of (d), in the SAME framework as (a)+(b)+action (de Vries 2017). Held at 0.73: the expansion uses pre-allocated 'spare' slots rather than truly unbounded growth (the Bayesian-nonparametric entry, Fox 2011, covers the unbounded case).
failure_signatures: Expansion engages pre-allocated unused slots in a fixed-dimension state space rather than unbounded growth -- truly open-ended latent cardinality needs Bayesian nonparametrics (HDP-HMM).
No residue/non-erasure primitive: model reduction PRUNES redundant structure (the opposite of non-erasure), so this formalism actively erases rather than preserving an unresolved trace.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Structure learning is an emergent property of active inference: model expansion adds novel hidden states to explain new observations, and Bayesian model reduction merges states / prunes complexity, yielding birth, merge and death of latent causes within one generative model.
mapping.ree_translation: DLIF capacity (c) -- latent-node birth/death/merge/split -- is not a missing mathematics requiring a new object; it is realised in active inference via expansion + Bayesian model reduction. The DLIF 'infer latent nodes / merge / split / reweight offline' capacity (research-map item, and the toy's consolidation step) maps directly onto this.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Delivers (c) and partial (d). Crucially for the ANSWERED-POSITIVE branch: this formalism PRUNES redundant structure, which is the OPPOSITE of REE's residue/non-erasure -- confirming residue is the one capacity not covered, and that it must be shown separable (ARC-013 V3-EXQ-587), not assumed.
mapping.source_context: Computational-neuroscience model of human concept learning; simulated agent.

confidence_components.notes: Strong, well-cited demonstration with the exact birth/merge/death vocabulary. Transfer risk moderate: REE's hippocampal candidacy/merge machinery is a different mechanism, so this is an existence proof that (c) lives in AI, not that REE implements it identically.
